finding.claim: Unchecked type assertion in deepSet panics on attacker-controlled deepObject query keys; nothing recovers panics in non-test code, so a panic propagates from the validator.
finding.source: Query string on an operation with a deepObject, explode:true object parameter, e.g. ?filter[a]=1&filter[a][b]=2 (req_resp_decoder.go:686-711, reached via validate_request.go:83, :181, :267).
finding.sink: req_resp_decoder.go:929 m = m[key].(map[string]any) in deepSet (:923-932), called from makeObject (:945) via DecodeObject (:722).

trace.note: ValidateRequest iterates operation parameters and calls ValidateParameter
decodeValue dispatches to DecodeObject for object-typed parameters
deepObject propsFn collects keys matching ^param[ and joins bracket segments with \x1F
makeObject called with the props map
props iterated in random map order
only values are checked for the delimiter; keys are not
when key 'a' already holds a string, unchecked assertion panics

finding.guards_checked: Delimiter check in makeObject (:940) covers values only. deepSet has no type check. No recover() in non-test code (grep). No test covers conflicting deepObject keys. Not executed; traced from source. Impact is per-request: net/http recovers per connection, but callers running validation outside net/http's recovery could crash the process. Reachable unauthenticated when the route has no security requirement.

finding.claim: RejectWhenRequestBodyNotSpecified is bypassed by chunked request bodies because the check uses ContentLength > 0, which is -1 for chunked requests.
finding.source: HTTP request with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and a body, sent to an operation with no requestBody (validate_request.go:93 gate, opt-in via options.RejectWhenRequestBodyNotSpecified).
finding.sink: validate_request.go:105 check on input.Request.ContentLength; the body is never read or rejected on this path.

trace.note: body validation block entered when ExcludeRequestBody is false
ContentLength > 0 test; chunked requests have ContentLength -1, so the test is false

finding.guards_checked: Only the ContentLength > 0 test exists. No fallback for ContentLength -1 or for a non-nil Body. Logic reasoning from Go net/http semantics; not executed.
finding.repro: Enable RejectWhenRequestBodyNotSpecified; send POST with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and a non-empty body to an operation with no requestBody; observe that no RequestError is returned.

finding.claim: Only the first occurrence of a repeated scalar query, header, cookie, form, or multipart key is validated; later occurrences are neither validated nor rejected.
finding.source: Repeated key in the request, e.g. ?id=1&id=<bad>, a duplicate header, a duplicate cookie, or a duplicate multipart/form field.
finding.sink: Schema validation of the decoded value (validate_request.go:250, :364) covers only the first occurrence; handlers reading all occurrences receive unchecked values.

trace.note: DecodePrimitive picks the first non-empty value (:524-532) and parses only it (:537)
DecodeArray with explode:false keeps values[:1] unless the first value contains the delimiter
DecodeObject form explode uses values[0] for each key
cookie DecodePrimitive uses req.Cookie(param), the first cookie

finding.guards_checked: No rejection of multiple values for scalar slots in styled paths. Contrast: content-based path rejects multiples for non-query parameters (:176-179) and validates all query values as an array (:212-228). Explode array path parses all values (:576-601). Impact is conditional: exploitable only if the handler reads occurrences beyond the first. Not executed; traced from source.
